preamble: Click-type merger: the postalveolar (alveolar) click [ǃ] is realized as a dental click [ǀ]. In Sowetan (urban Johannesburg) Zulu, the standard contrast between dental and postalveolar clicks is lost and the two occur as free variants in both directions (Gunnink 2014, cited in Sands & Gunnink 2019). Sands & Gunnink attribute this to contact with Sotho, which has a single click type, and with clickless Pedi and Tswana. Wikipedia's Sotho article separately states, without forms, that Sesotho postalveolar clicks tend to be replaced by dental clicks in ordinary speech. Only one clear Zulu form shows the ǃ > ǀ direction, so certainty is 2.

languageExamples.context: Free variation in both directions (-ǃala ~ -ǀala); Sands & Gunnink (2019) link it to contact with Sotho

examples.note: Reverse substitution also occurs: -ǀela 'request' (cela) can be -ǃela (Sands & Gunnink 2019).
